title: pricing-packaging-back-of-envelope-notes-v13
content:
Notes: pricing / packaging back-of-envelope (scratchpad)
Owner: Ethan Kim
Date: 2025-11-20 (iter v13)
Collaborators: Maya Chen, Liam O'Connor
Status: draft / thinking-out-loud

Goals: quick unit economics to validate a few tier ideas for hosted API (PLG + paid tiers) and Dedicated entry pricing. Focus on token math, margin targets, and simple conversion assumptions.

Assumptions (baseline)
- Infra cost per GPU-hour (amortized across infra + ops + network + storage): $4.00 / GPU-hr (weighted avg across fleet)
- Average tokens per second (TPS) per GPU depends on model and context length. Pick a few model families:
  * small-open: 7B quant -> ~1500 tps (simple serving)
  * med-open: 13B quant -> ~700 tps
  * large-open: 70B -> ~120 tps
  * prod-llm (opt or commercial) baseline for hosted: assume equivalent to med-open for pricing exercise
- Token composition: 85% completions tokens (billable) + 15% prompt tokens on average (depends on prompt length)
- Average request latency SLO influences batching; assume we can batch to 80% GPU utilization for PLG traffic, burstable to 95% for Dedicated customers.

Rough per-token infra cost (back-of-envelope)
Method A: cost via GPU-hours -> tokens per GPU-hour * hourly cost
- tokens_per_sec * 3600 = tokens_per_hour
- cost_per_token = gpu_hour_cost / tokens_per_hour

Compute numbers (approx):
1) small-open (1500 tps) -> 1500 * 3600 = 5.4M tokens/hr -> cost_per_token = 4 / 5.4e6 = $7.4e-7 (~0.00000074) -> $0.00074 per 1k tokens
2) med-open (700 tps) -> 700 * 3600 = 2.52M tokens/hr -> cost_per_token = 4 / 2.52e6 = $1.587e-6 (~0.0000016) -> $0.0016 per 1k tokens
3) large-open (120 tps) -> 120 * 3600 = 432k tokens/hr -> cost_per_token = 4 / 432k = $9.26e-6 -> $0.00926 per 1k tokens

Notes: above is *inference compute only* (GPU). Need to add overhead (storage, networking, management, licensing, support). Factor-of-3 rule-of-thumb for full landed cost (so multiply GPU-only by 3x) to get variable cost. Also include margin target and free tier/subsidy.

Applying 3x overhead:
- small-open: $0.00074 * 3 = $0.00222 per 1k tokens
- med-open: $0.0016 * 3 = $0.0048 per 1k tokens
- large-open: $0.00926 * 3 = $0.0278 per 1k tokens

Target gross margin (hosted): 60%+ for PLG; enterprise/Reserved can be lower but compensated by contract value/support. So suggested price (list) = cost / (1 - margin)
- for med-open target price (60% margin): price = 0.0048 / 0.4 = 0.012 -> $0.012 per 1k tokens
- round/pricing psychology -> $0.01 per 1k tokens for med-open baseline (keeps price competitive vs incumbents).

Compare to market: many providers charge $0.03-$0.06 per 1k for comparable open models (or more for commercial models). Our cost calc seems plausible to undercut while preserving margin given scale. But key sensitivity = throughput (tps) and utilization. If utilization drops to 40% for small accounts, cost doubles. Need to model low-utilization tail.

Tier ideas (sketch)
- Free tier: 100k tokens / month (onboarding), lower SLOs, standard models only (small-open). Purpose: product led signup + prompt engineering for customers.
- Starter / Indie: $10 / month -> includes 2M prompt+completion tokens (round to 2M), rate limits 10 rps, 1 seat. Effective price = $10 / 2M = $0.005 per 1k tokens -> subsidized, but conversion lever as usage grows.
- Team: $200 / month -> 50M tokens included -> $0.004 per 1k tokens incl (plus overage at list). Bundled features: multi-seat, basic analytics, retention 30d.
- Business: $2,000 / month -> 1.2B tokens included -> $0.0017 per 1k tokens. SLA, dedicated routing priority, mini-dedicated pool option.
- Enterprise / Dedicated: committed reserved capacity pricing (monthly/annual). Example: reserved 1x A100-equivalent GPU pool for $X/month (calculate below). Include uplift for support & onboarding.

Reserved capacity quick calc (Dedicated)
- If 1 x GPU-month cost (infra + ops + amortized infra) = say $4/hr * 24 * 30 = $2880 GPU-month (just GPU-only) -> apply 3x overhead = $8640/month. Add margin and enterprise premium -> list price ~ $10k - $12k / GPU-mo.
- We can offer smaller units (vCPU-equivalent or qps) but simpler to sell in GPU-pools. Pricing bands: 1 GPU = $11k/mo, 4 GPU = $40k/mo (volume discounts). Include burst pricing for hosted fallback.

Overage / metering rules
- Bill on prompt+completion tokens (standard). Possible add per-request charge for very short responses to avoid tiny-call inefficiency.
- Offer committed bucket (flat included tokens) + pay-as-you-go overage at list price.

Conversion assumptions / funnel (PLG)
- Free -> Starter: 3% conversion (conservative)
- Starter -> paid-move-up: 12% over 6 months
- Avg usage per Starter converting user in month 1: 6M tokens

P&L sensitivity quicks
- Key levers: model choice (tps), utilization (batching), average context length (prompt share), price per 1k tokens, overhead multiplier.
- Example sensitivity: if utilization falls from 80% -> 40%, cost per 1k doubles, price must double to preserve margin. Means low-usage tail kills unit economics for small plans unless we subsidize via higher-priced teams/enterprise.

Open questions / TODOs
- Need empirical tps numbers from serving-runtime team for common models (13B, 30B, 70B) under typical request distributions (ctx len 1k avg).
- Confirm overhead multiplier (3x) with finance (includes SRE, infra, data egress, CDN, storage).
- Decide if we peg pricing to model classes (small/med/large) or abstract by capability tiers (standard, high-accuracy, long-context) to reduce cognitive load.
- Explore bundling with Redwood Optimize (auto-quantize suggestions) to reduce effective cost for customers (value-add + product differentiation).

Quick toy scenarios (for product discussion)
- Scenario A: PLG at $10/mo starter; 1000 starters -> MRR $10k. If 3% convert free->starter, need X signups to reach 1k starters. Not huge. But need active usage to justify margins.
- Scenario B: Team tier $200/mo with 50M tokens included - ideal for early SaaS customers using embeddings + chat. 500 teams -> $100k MRR -> good scale.

Notes to self:
- Keep list prices round and simple ($0.01/1k, $0.005/1k, $10/mo, etc.) and present how underlying unit economics maps to them.
- Prepare slide with cost curves by utilization and model family (x-axis utilization 20-100%, y-axis cost per 1k tokens) for product meeting.

End of scratchpad. This is rough. Will refine after getting real tps numbers and finance overhead confirmation.

Keywords: token math, unit economics, PLG tiers, reserved capacity, utilization sensitivity, bundling
